title: Greenleaf Insurance - data usage & no-train commitment
meeting_header: 2025-10-07 15:00 PT | Duration: 52m | Recording: Fireflies | Attendees: Lena, Marco, Priya / Nina, Ethan, Raji, Aaron
summary: Customer needed explicit confirmation on data handling: retention of prompts/contexts, PII/PHI handling, ability to opt-out of model training, KMS/HSM key management, audit logs and export for legal hold. Redwood AE/SE walked through platform controls, default retention behavior, RBAC/SSO options, and provided follow-ups (SOC2 report, retention config doc, example audit export).
topics: audit logs, export and legal hold
data residency and private deployment options
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we scheduled 50 minutes, we can run a bit over if needed. I'm Lena, I'm the AE on your account. Marco our SE is here to go through the technical controls. Priya from compliance is here too. Could you all introduce?
[00:10] Nina Patel: Hi I'm Nina, Head of Data Privacy at Greenleaf. We're primarily worried about claims data and potential PHI - want to understand prompts retention and training guarantees.
[00:18] Marco Diaz: Great, thanks Nina. Quick note — we recorded this for notes. I'll try to keep timestamps, and apologies in advance for any transcription noise.
[00:25] Ethan Cole: Ethan, Cloud Architect. We'd like to know KMS specifics and whether keys can be customer-managed/HSM-backed. Also curious about audit log exports for e-discovery.
[00:33] Raji Menon: Raji, Security Engineer. Two high level asks: 1) is customer data ever used to update models? 2) what logs are available and how long retained by default?
[00:41] Aaron Liu: Aaron, Legal. We'll want a written no-training commitment and usual contract language.
[00:46] Marco Diaz: Cool. I'll start with the short version: for Redwood Hosted, by default we do not train on customer data — we have a contractual no-training clause for enterprise customers and an operational control that prevents customer data from being added into model training pipelines. We do keep transient context for inference caching but those caches are ephemeral and TTL-based.
[01:05] Nina Patel: When you say ephemeral, can you quantify? Is that minutes, hours? Where is that stored?
[01:10] Marco Diaz: Good question. The default KV cache TTL is 1 hour for hosted; it's in-memory on the serving node unless configured otherwise. For Dedicated and Private deployments you control cache behavior; on Private it never leaves your VPC.
[01:23] Priya Rao: Are prompts logged to disk for debugging? We need assurance that raw prompts with PHI aren't persisted longer than necessary.
[01:31] Marco Diaz: By default we persist request/response pairs for 30 days for metrics and troubleshooting. That's configurable for enterprise customers — we can shorten to 7 days or disable storage entirely and only keep aggregated telemetry. If you need write-only ephemeral mode, Dedicated/Private gives that guarantee.
[01:47] Nina Patel: So hosted customers get 30 days default but can request change? Will that be reflected in policy language?
[01:54] Lena Park: Yes, we'll put that in the SOW and add a retention_config section to your contract. We can set retention to 0 days for request bodies for an enterprise commitment, with exceptions for legal holds.
[02:05] Aaron Liu: Legal holds are important. If we need to preserve certain requests for litigation or regulatory inquiry, what's the mechanism?
[02:11] Marco Diaz: We support export of audit logs and raw request payloads on demand. There's an API to request an export; for longer-term needs we can arrange object storage exports to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules you control. Exports are signed and encrypted in transit.
[02:25] Ethan Cole: Regarding encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM-backed keys? Any FIPS compliance?
[02:32] Priya Rao: Also are keys stored by Redwood or can we bring our own?
[02:36] Marco Diaz: For Hosted we support BYOK with major cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google CMEK, Azure Key Vault). Keys can be HSM-backed on supported clouds; Redwood stores only the encrypted key material pointer. For Private deployments you can run a local HSM and Redwood's control plane can be configured to use it. We also have a FIPS-compatible path in our encryption libraries — Priya, we can share the FIPS attestation notes.
[02:56] Nina Patel: Can you confirm encrypted-at-rest and in-transit by default?
[03:00] Marco Diaz: Yes TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest by default, and CMEK/BYOK for customer-managed scenarios.
[03:06] Raji Menon: Audit logs: what granularity? Do we get token-level, request headers, user identity? How long?
[03:13] Marco Diaz: Audit logs include timestamp, API route, user identity or service principal, redwood tenant id, model served, request id, latency, and status. By default audit logs are retained 365 days but again configurable. Sensitive fields like request body and response body are stored per your retention policy; they can be excluded from logs entirely.
[03:32] Aaron Liu: On legal/process side, will you sign a clause that you won't use customer data to improve models? We need it explicit.
[03:38] Lena Park: Absolutely — we have a standard no-training clause that we put in enterprise agreements. For extra assurance we can include operational attestations and SOC 2 controls that map to the process.
[03:47] Nina Patel: Speaking of SOC 2, do you offer SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates? Any pen test reports?
[03:53] Priya Rao: Also supply chain / subcontractor list — who has access to logs?
[03:58] Marco Diaz: We have SOC 2 Type II; ISO 27001 at company level is in process — Priya, I'll send current certificates. Pen test summaries are available under NDA. Access is role-based — engineering has access in production support cases, but access is audited. For enterprise, you can restrict support access and enable live session approvals.
[04:18] Ethan Cole: For SSO/identity, do you support SAML, OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning? RBAC roles for teams?
[04:24] Marco Diaz: Yes SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for groups and role sync. RBAC is fine-grained — admin, developer, billing, read-only auditor. You can bind roles to groups via SCIM.
[04:33] Raji Menon: How do you handle service accounts — are they scoped? We don't want wide access tokens floating around.
[04:38] Marco Diaz: We issue scoped API keys with route-level restrictions and expiration. We also support token rotation and short-lived credentials if you integrate with your identity provider.
[04:47] Nina Patel: About PII and PHI — do you offer automatic redaction/PII detection? Or should we be doing redaction on our side?
[04:55] Marco Diaz: We offer an optional pre-processing redaction step through our content-scan hooks; it can run in-line or as a pre-inference pipeline. We provide regex and ML-based detectors for common PII fields; for PHI we recommend you apply application-side redaction as well. For high assurance customers we can help tune detectors for your domain.
[05:12] Priya Rao: If we redacted at edge, but still include structured metadata in payloads, is there any risk of that metadata being used?
[05:18] Marco Diaz: That metadata is treated like other request attributes — it's included in logs only if configured. We can mark fields as sensitive so they're never written to disk.
[05:26] Aaron Liu: On the no-training point, operationally how is that enforced? Is it just a contract or is there a technical guardrail?
[05:32] Marco Diaz: Both. Technically, training pipelines are isolated and there's a curated data ingress process with approvals and audit trails; customer data is excluded unless explicitly approved and processed under a separate onboarding. We can provide the data flow diagram and controls as part of the security package.
[05:47] Nina Patel: Can you describe the data flow diagram in plain terms? For instance, where does request body travel from our client to the model and where might any copies exist?
[05:56] Marco Diaz: Sure. For Hosted: Client -> TLS -> Edge proxy -> Router -> Serving node. Serving nodes keep ephemeral in-memory KV for inference and optionally write request/response to encrypted object storage (if retention enabled). Audit logs stream to our logging cluster (encrypted). Exports to customer S3 are possible. For Dedicated/Private the data path stays in your VPC and control plane only holds metadata.
[06:20] Ethan Cole: For private deployments, what constraints exist on upgrades and patching? Who has access to upgrade images?
[06:26] Marco Diaz: We push signed images; upgrades are initiated by the customer's ops team in Private deployments. Redwood provides signed packages and can assist with patch windows. Access to images is through our build pipeline, all artifacts are signed and checksummed.
[06:39] Priya Rao: Can you provide an example audit export? We want to feed it into our SIEM.
[06:45] Marco Diaz: Yes we'll send a sample JSON schema and a sample export file. We'll include fields mapping to Splunk/Datadog.
[06:51] Nina Patel: About data residency — we need EU-only for certain lines of business. Can you guarantee region pinning and that data won't be replicated outside the region?
[06:59] Marco Diaz: Yes region pinning is supported. For hosted we have EU regions and we'll ensure tenancy and storage are in-region. For absolute control we recommend Dedicated in-region or Private.
[07:10] Aaron Liu: What about third-party subprocessors — do you publish a list? Any Chinese or other foreign subcontractors we should be aware of?
[07:17] Marco Diaz: We publish a subprocessors list. None are located in restricted jurisdictions for our EU accounts; we'll attach the latest list.
[07:24] Lena Park: Quick check — are we missing anything major from compliance perspective?
[07:28] Priya Rao: Data minimization process details, and an explanation of how you handle developer access to logs for debugging.
[07:34] Marco Diaz: Developer access requires a production support workflow — ephemeral time-limited access with just-in-time approvals; all sessions recorded.
[07:41] Nina Patel: For the no-train clause, Aaron wants written language. We'll need the exact wording and whether it's standard or addendum.
[07:48] Lena Park: We'll provide standard no-training addendum language and can add additional operational attestations if you want.
[07:54] Aaron Liu: Also want to know about breach notification timelines and contact process.
[07:58] Marco Diaz: We have 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents; we also provide updates via your security contact and runbooks for incident response.
[08:07] Ethan Cole: Can we require SIEM integration in the contract?
[08:10] Lena Park: Yes we can include SIEM export and sample schema in SOW.
[08:14] Nina Patel: Anything about model artifacts? If Redwood releases new model versions, could there be any inference drift or leakage related to customer's previous prompts?
[08:23] Marco Diaz: Models are versioned. We never incorporate customer prompt data into base model checkpoints unless customers opt-in to a data sharing program. We also offer model pinning to freeze the model version served.
[08:36] Priya Rao: For auditability, can you provide an access log per user per request? We need lines in our audit that show which internal Redwood identity looked at logs and when.
[08:45] Marco Diaz: Yes, we can provide both access audit and content access audit. They are part of the audit export.
[08:52] Raji Menon: A few nitty-gritty items: do you hash request ids? Is there PII in your logging schema by default?
[08:58] Marco Diaz: Request ids are GUIDs. By default we do not hash ids but we can enable hashing or tokenization on request. PII is not logged unless enabled; request/response bodies are excluded by default in the stricter enterprise profile.
[09:12] Nina Patel: What about test datasets — sometimes support uses synthetic transcripts. How are those tagged?
[09:18] Marco Diaz: Support test data is labeled and separated from production. All synthetic or replayed data has an origin tag and is excluded from analytics for training.
[09:26] Aaron Liu: Can we get a written attestation that no support engineer will use raw prompts for debugging without explicit approval?
[09:32] Marco Diaz: Yes, we can add that operational control — support must get ticket-level approval and all access is recorded.
[09:37] Lena Park: I'll summarize next steps at the end; but Marco will send SOC 2 and pen test NDA, a retention options doc, sample audit export, and no-train clause text.
[09:47] Marco Diaz: I'll make a list. Also note, one practical item: if you want zero retention for request bodies on hosted, we recommend dedicated logging endpoints to avoid accidentally routing debug traffic to persisted stores.
[09:58] Ethan Cole: Understood. For SSO and SCIM provisioning, do you support group filter rules?
[10:03] Marco Diaz: Yes group filter rules and attribute mapping are supported.
[10:07] Nina Patel: A quick question on monitoring: can we get token-level cost telemetry per team?
[10:12] Priya Rao: We want billing split by line of business as well.
[10:16] Lena Park: Redwood Console supports token-level breakdowns and per-team cost allocation; we'll include an example export.
[10:25] Aaron Liu: If we set retention 0 days, and then later need data for an audit that occurred earlier, is there any way to retroactively recover?
[10:33] Marco Diaz: No — 0-day retention deletes request bodies immediately; the only mechanism is if you explicitly set up export or retention for legal hold. That's why legal hold export is part of the workflow.
[10:45] Nina Patel: Can you walk through the legal hold flow?
[10:48] Marco Diaz: Legal hold flow: Customer opens request via portal -> identify scope (tenant, timeframe, request-ids) -> we prepare export to your secure bucket -> we lock objects and provide checksum and manifest -> you confirm receipt. For hosted customers with 0-day retention, legal hold must be initiated before deletion schedule runs.
[11:05] Raji Menon: How are exports authenticated?
[11:08] Marco Diaz: Exports are signed, encrypted, and delivered to pre-authorized destination (customer S3 with bucket policy). We can also do VPC peering or a dedicate transfer node.
[11:18] Priya Rao: On the SOC 2 attestations, can we map CCs to our internal controls?
[11:24] Marco Diaz: Yes we'll provide control mappings and a SOC 2 bridge document for you to map to your control set.
[11:31] Ethan Cole: Any per-request redaction APIs look like? Latency impact?
[11:35] Marco Diaz: Inline redaction typically adds 40–120ms depending on models and rule sets; you can run redaction in a preprocessing job to avoid adding to inference latency.
[11:46] Nina Patel: Are there sandbox/test tenants for integration testing that mimic logs but do not contain live PII?
[11:51] Marco Diaz: Yes, we provide isolated sandbox tenants with synthetic data and separate logging buckets.
[11:58] Aaron Liu: We will need to review the standard no-training addendum and the retention language. Also we'd like a clause for breach notification SLA and a dedicated security contact.
[12:08] Lena Park: We'll include that. Any other items?
[12:11] Nina Patel: One last ask — can you provide example contract language that specifically states "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, improve or adapt models without Customer's explicit written consent"?
[12:22] Marco Diaz: Yes that's in our addendum; we'll share verbatim text.
[12:26] Priya Rao: Also want to see your access logs schema again.
[12:29] Marco Diaz: I'll attach schemas.
[12:32] Lena Park: Ok let's do quick recap and next steps.
[12:35] Lena Park: Recap: Redwood confirms default hosted retention = 30 days, configurable. No-training is a contractual and technical commitment. BYOK/CMEK supported, HSM possible on Private, audit logs and exports available, region pinning supported, SSO/SCIM/RBAC supported, legal hold export workflow exists. Next steps: Marco to share SOC2, pen test NDA, retention options, sample audit export, and no-train clause. Lena to follow-up with SOW language and include SIEM export. Customer to confirm preferred retention and whether they want hosted vs dedicated for EU-only requirements.
[12:59] Nina Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll review and revert with a list of lines of business that need EU residency and whether we want retention zeroed.
[13:07] Lena Park: Thank you all. We'll target sending artifacts by EOD next Tuesday.
[13:12] Marco Diaz: Thanks, bye.
[13:15] [END]
